statement: Acupuncture produces a moderate effect over no-treatment (~0.5 SD) but only a small effect over sham/placebo needling (~0.2 SD) for chronic pain (back/neck, osteoarthritis, headache, shoulder), with effects persisting ~12 months; most of the benefit is context/ritual/placebo, not point-specific.
effect_size: ~0.5 SD vs no-acupuncture; ~0.2 SD vs sham; ~15% decay at 1 year
population: 39 high-quality RCTs / ~20,827 chronic-pain patients (individual patient data)

provenance.primary: Vickers et al., Arch Intern Med 2012; update J Pain 2018

confidence_notes: Grade: works-for-some-things. The sham-vs-real gap is the truth serum; small real specific effect, large placebo/counter-irritation component. Not evidence for non-pain indications.

statement: Acupuncture/acupressure at the PC6 point reduces post-operative and chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting — the most robust specific (non-placebo-explained) acupuncture effect.
effect_size: Significant reduction in PONV/CINV vs control
population: Cochrane PC6 antiemesis reviews (Lee et al.)

provenance.primary: Lee A et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev (PC6 acupoint stimulation for nausea/vomiting)

confidence_notes: Grade: works-for-some-things. One of the few acupuncture signals that survives decent blinding.

statement: The traditional acupuncture framework (qi flowing through meridians) corresponds to no known anatomical structure; sham/non-penetrating needling at 'wrong' points works almost as well as 'real' acupuncture, refuting point-specificity and the meridian theory.
effect_size: Sham ≈ verum in most blinded trials

provenance.primary: Multiple sham-controlled RCTs; synthesized in Ernst & Singh, Trick or Treatment 2008

confidence_notes: Grade: no-evidence (the theory). Mechanism is plausibly diffuse noxious inhibitory control + placebo, not qi/meridians.

statement: St John's Wort (Hypericum perforatum) extracts are superior to placebo and about as effective as standard antidepressants for mild-to-moderate major depression, with fewer side-effect dropouts than SSRIs.
effect_size: Response rates ~ equal to SSRIs (e.g. 52% vs 52%); fewer adverse-effect dropouts (OR ~0.53)

provenance.primary: Linde K et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2008, CD000448.pub3

confidence_notes: Grade: works (narrow). German-language trials skewed more positive (heterogeneity caveat). Restricted to mild-moderate depression.

statement: St John's Wort is a potent CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inducer that can reduce efficacy of oral contraceptives, warfarin, ciclosporin, and HIV antiretrovirals, and can precipitate serotonin syndrome with SSRIs/SNRIs.
effect_size: Clinically significant loss of drug levels; documented transplant rejection and contraceptive failure cases

provenance.primary: Pharmacology literature; summarized in CAM reviews

confidence_notes: Grade: harmful (interactions). The most-cited 'natural is not safe' example: a real antidepressant that is also a dangerous enzyme inducer.

statement: Enteric-coated peppermint oil (a smooth-muscle antispasmodic) improves global symptoms and abdominal pain in irritable bowel syndrome vs placebo.
effect_size: RR ~2.4 for global symptom improvement

provenance.primary: Alammar N et al., BMC Complement Altern Med 2019 (peppermint oil IBS meta-analysis)

confidence_notes: Grade: works. In mainstream gastroenterology guidance. Main side-effect: reflux.

statement: Ginger is a modest, real antiemetic for pregnancy-related nausea and as an adjunct for post-operative and chemotherapy-induced nausea.
effect_size: Moderate reduction in nausea; not a cure

provenance.primary: Multiple RCT meta-analyses (ginger for nausea of pregnancy / chemotherapy)

confidence_notes: Grade: works-for-some-things (nausea only).

statement: Curcumin (turmeric) has strong in-vitro anti-inflammatory mechanism but near-zero oral bioavailability; human trials in osteoarthritis are small, short, on subjective/surrogate endpoints, often industry-linked and using enhanced formulations, so the 'natural anti-inflammatory' outcome claim remains unproven.
effect_size: Some OA pain trials ~ on par with NSAIDs but low quality

provenance.primary: Curcumin OA RCTs + bioavailability literature (Nelson et al., J Med Chem 2017 'curcumin is a PAINS/IMPS')

confidence_notes: Grade: no-evidence -> emerging. Mechanism is real; outcome claim outruns the evidence.

statement: Saw palmetto (Serenoa repens) is no better than placebo for lower-urinary-tract symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia, even at double and triple doses.
effect_size: AUASI change 0.68 (saw palmetto) vs 0.72 (placebo) at 12 mo — no clinical difference

provenance.primary: Bent S et al., NEJM 2006 (STEP); Franco JVA et al., Cochrane 2023

confidence_notes: Grade: placebo-level (settled). Case study in how early low-quality positive trials evaporate under rigorous design.

statement: Ginkgo biloba does not prevent dementia, Alzheimer's disease, or cognitive decline in older adults.
effect_size: No reduction in dementia incidence over ~6 years

provenance.primary: DeKosky ST et al. (Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory / GEM), JAMA 2008

confidence_notes: Grade: placebo-level / no-evidence for the headline claim.

statement: The explanatory theories of Traditional Chinese Medicine (qi, meridians, five phases) and Ayurveda (doshas, five elements) are pre-scientific models that make no falsifiable physiology-level predictions that survive testing — they are not descriptions of biology.
effect_size: No measurable correspondence between traditional diagnoses (pulse/tongue->dosha) and disease states

provenance.primary: Ernst & Singh, Trick or Treatment 2008; general scientific critique

confidence_notes: Grade: no-evidence (the system). Separate from the pharmacology of individual compounds — same standard applied to any historical medical system.

statement: Some compounds in traditional pharmacopeias have real pharmacology (e.g. artemisinin from Artemisia annua, a TCM remedy, now a frontline WHO antimalarial; ephedrine from ma huang), but the validated win is the isolated, purified, dosed, and trialled molecule — not a vindication of qi or doshas.
effect_size: Artemisinin: Nobel Prize 2015 (Tu Youyou); frontline antimalarial

provenance.primary: Tu Youyou, Nobel Lecture 2015; artemisinin clinical literature

confidence_notes: Tradition as a source of leads is provenance, not proof (SCHEMA hard rule). The molecule, validated by modern method, is the evidence.

statement: About 1 in 5 Ayurvedic medicines (US- and Indian-manufactured, bought via the Internet) contain detectable lead, mercury, or arsenic; rasa shastra products (which intentionally combine herbs with metals) are worse (~40%), and metal-containing products exceeded acceptable daily-intake limits.
effect_size: ~20% of products with Pb/Hg/As; ~40% of rasa shastra products

provenance.primary: Saper RB et al., JAMA 2008

confidence_notes: Grade: harmful. Documented lead-poisoning clusters traced to these products. Distinct toxicology hazard, separate from efficacy.

statement: Spinal manipulative therapy (SMT) produces modest short-term pain and function improvement for acute and chronic non-specific low-back pain — about the same as other recommended active therapies (exercise, NSAIDs, physiotherapy), not superior to them.
effect_size: Small benefit; clinically similar to other active treatments
population: Cochrane / Rubinstein systematic reviews of LBP RCTs

provenance.primary: Rubinstein SM et al., BMJ 2019 (SMT for chronic LBP SR/meta)

confidence_notes: Grade: works-for-some-things. A reasonable option within guideline care, not magic. Cross-ref Section 21 (back pain).

statement: The chiropractic 'vertebral subluxation' that allegedly impedes 'Innate Intelligence' and causes systemic/visceral disease is not visible on imaging, has no demonstrated pathophysiology, and spinal adjustment does not treat internal disease (asthma, ear infections, hypertension, immune function).
effect_size: No supported effect on non-musculoskeletal disease

provenance.primary: Ernst E, critical reviews of chiropractic; Trick or Treatment 2008

confidence_notes: Grade: no-evidence. Must be graded separately from evidence-based SMT for back pain.

statement: Cervical (neck) high-velocity manipulation is associated with cervical artery (vertebral/carotid) dissection causing stroke; absolute per-manipulation risk is low and the causal fraction is debated (reverse causation possible), but the catastrophic consequence and modest, replaceable benefit make the risk-benefit unfavourable for neck pain.
effect_size: Rare (order ~1 in tens-of-thousands to millions of manipulations); causality debated

provenance.primary: Cassidy JD et al., Spine 2008 (population-based, reverse-causation argument); neurology case literature

confidence_notes: Grade: works-for-some-things with a load-bearing safety caveat. Prefer lower-risk options (exercise, mobilisation) for the neck.

statement: Reiki, Therapeutic Touch, and other 'energy healing' modalities show no specific effect beyond placebo in sham-controlled trials, and the postulated human 'energy field' has never been demonstrated — practitioners could not detect it above chance.
effect_size: No detection of 'energy field' above chance; no specific clinical effect vs sham
population: Emily Rosa Therapeutic Touch experiment + sham-controlled trials

provenance.primary: Rosa L, Rosa E, Sarner L, Barrett S, JAMA 1998

confidence_notes: Grade: placebo-level. Benefit is relaxation/attention/human contact, not the claimed mechanism. Contrast with meditation/yoga/tai chi (works) in F2.

statement: Homeopathy is chemically empty (typical 30C remedies contain on average not a single molecule of the original substance, violating Avogadro/stoichiometry) and shows no effect beyond placebo across the clinical literature — a settled scientific verdict, not an open question.
effect_size: Effects consistent with placebo; shrink toward null as trial quality rises
population: Shang Lancet meta-analysis; NHMRC review of 176 studies / 61 conditions; UK House of Commons S&T 2010

provenance.primary: Shang A et al., Lancet 2005; NHMRC Australia 2015 Information Paper

confidence_notes: Grade: placebo-level (settled). NHMRC 2015: 'no health conditions for which there is reliable evidence that homeopathy is effective.' Danger = opportunity cost when used instead of real treatment.

statement: Naturopathy and 'functional medicine' bundle genuinely evidence-based lifestyle counselling (diet, exercise, sleep, stress) with unvalidated testing (IgG food-sensitivity, 'adrenal fatigue', hair mineral analysis) and unproven treatments (high-dose IV vitamins, chelation for non-poisoning, prolonged antibiotics for 'chronic Lyme') — each must be graded on its own merits.
effect_size: Lifestyle half: real; proprietary testing/treatment half: no-evidence to harmful

provenance.primary: Offit PA, Do You Believe in Magic? 2013; NCCIH; specific-test critiques

confidence_notes: Grade: mixed. 'Functional medicine' is an organisational/marketing category, not an evidentiary tier. Keep the lifestyle advice, decline the proprietary tests.

statement: Placebo produces measurable changes in subjective, brain-mediated outcomes (pain via naloxone-reversible endogenous opioids, nausea, fatigue, mood) but has little reliable effect on objective/binary outcomes (tumour size, infection, blood glucose, fracture healing, arterial patency) — it modulates the experience of illness, not the pathology.
effect_size: Real effect on subjective outcomes; little reliable effect on objective outcomes vs no-treatment
population: Hrobjartsson & Gotzsche analysis of placebo-vs-no-treatment trials

provenance.primary: Hrobjartsson A, Gotzsche PC, NEJM 2001 ('Is the placebo powerless?'); Cochrane update 2010

confidence_notes: The bounding principle: a placebo-only modality can be humane comfort alongside real care, lethal substitute instead of it.

statement: Patients who chose alternative medicine as the SOLE treatment for curable breast/prostate/lung/colorectal cancer had ~55% vs 78% 5-year survival (HR 2.50 overall, HR 5.68 for breast); a companion study showed 'complementary' medicine users were far more likely to refuse conventional treatment, and once refusal was accounted for, the excess mortality disappeared — i.e. the harm is the displacement of proven care, not CAM alongside it.
effect_size: HR 2.50 (alternative as sole Rx); HR 5.68 breast; excess mortality mediated by treatment refusal
population: Johnson 2018: 281 alternative-medicine patients (JNCI) + complementary-medicine cohort (JAMA Oncol), NCDB curable cancers

provenance.primary: Johnson SB et al., JNCI 2018 (alternative, sole Rx) + JAMA Oncol 2018 (complementary + refusal)
provenance.surfaced_via: CAM chapter (30) build; cross-ref Section 25 oncology

confidence_notes: Grade: harmful (instead-of). The single most important CAM safety datum. Harm is overwhelmingly opportunity-cost, largest where conventional medicine works best. JAMA Oncol DOI 10.1001/jamaoncol.2018.2487.

statement: 'Natural' predicts nothing about safety, purity, dose, or interactions: herbs are unstandardised drugs (tenfold batch variation), supplements can be adulterated with undeclared pharmaceuticals, traditional metal-bearing preparations can poison, and the most dangerous interactions come from natural products (St John's Wort, ginkgo) taken alongside prescriptions.
effect_size: Real hepatotoxicity (kava, comfrey, green-tea-extract), interactions, contamination

provenance.primary: FDA adulteration reports; herb hepatotoxicity literature; Saper 2008 (metals)

confidence_notes: Foundational honesty rule. Hemlock, arsenic, aristolochic acid, amanita are all natural.

statement: Under the US Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (DSHEA, 1994), supplements, herbs, and homeopathic products reach the market without pre-market proof of efficacy, purity, or safety; the FDA must demonstrate harm after the fact — the structural cause of CAM-product contamination, mislabelling, and overstated claims.
effect_size: Post-market-only enforcement; 'sold in a pharmacy' is not evidence of testing

provenance.primary: DSHEA 1994 (Public Law 103-417); FDA guidance

confidence_notes: Regulation gap, not a clinical claim. Explains the supplement-aisle landscape.

statement: Co-locating an unproven therapy with a proven one ('integrative oncology', hospital acupuncture clinics) is an institutional choice, not an evidentiary upgrade; the fair, non-dismissive treatment of CAM is to grade each modality x indication on the same evidence ladder as everything else.
effect_size: Label is organisational, not evidentiary

provenance.primary: Corpus doctrine (06-evidence/SCHEMA.md); Ernst critiques of 'integrative medicine'

confidence_notes: The grade is the neutrality. CAM grades out as a patchwork: a few real narrow tools, a large middle of expensive placebo, a toxicology hazard at the edges, and one dangerous failure mode (instead-of).
